name: Urea cycle
summary: Liver. Starts in mitochondria — carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I (rate-limiting; NH₃ + HCO₃⁻ + 2 ATP → carbamoyl phosphate; needs N-acetylglutamate) and ornithine transcarbamylase — then finishes in the cytosol. Urea's two nitrogens: one from NH₃ (via carbamoyl phosphate), one from aspartate. “Ordinarily, Careless Crappers Are Also Frivolous About Urination.”

ornithine.name: Ornithine
ornithine.notes: Carried back into the mitochondrion to take up the next carbamoyl phosphate.

citrulline.name: Citrulline
citrulline.notes: Leaves the mitochondrion for the cytosolic steps.

arginine.name: Arginine
arginine.notes: Also the substrate for nitric oxide synthase (→ NO + citrulline).

otc.name: Ornithine transcarbamylase
otc.notes: Mitochondrial. Takes carbamoyl phosphate from CPS I. OTC deficiency is the most common urea cycle disorder (X-linked): hyperammonemia and ↑ orotic acid (excess carbamoyl phosphate spills into pyrimidine synthesis) with NO megaloblastic anemia — unlike UMP synthase deficiency.

ass.name: Argininosuccinate synthetase
ass.notes: Brings in the second nitrogen (aspartate). ATP → AMP + PPi (two high-energy bonds). Deficiency → citrullinemia.

asl.name: Argininosuccinate lyase
asl.notes: Releases fumarate, which links the urea cycle to the TCA cycle. Deficiency → argininosuccinic aciduria.

arginase.name: Arginase
arginase.notes: Cleaves off urea and regenerates ornithine. Deficiency → progressive spastic diplegia, ↑ arginine, milder hyperammonemia; treat with a low-arginine diet.
